1118.1: Raag Kedara, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mind, let us sing the Name of Ram (the Lord) every day. The Lord is beyond reach and beyond the senses, and cannot be perceived (by one's own wit); if the perfect Guru is met, he is made known. The servant on whom my Master himself has mercy is attuned in love to the Lord. Everyone does the Lord's devotion (in his own way), but he who pleases the Lord is the one accepted. The priceless Name of the Lord, Har Har, rests with the Lord (himself); when the Lord gives it, then the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is meditated on. He to whom my Master gives the Naam is released from his whole account. Those who worship the Lord's Name are called blessed servants; good fortune was written on their foreheads by the Lord from the start. Seeing them, my mind blossoms, as a son meeting his mother is clasped to her neck. We are (your) children, O Lord, my Father, my God: give me the understanding by which the Lord is found. As the cow rejoices on seeing her calf, so, O Nanak, (the servant) is clasped to the Lord's neck. ॥4॥
1118.2: Raag Kedara, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mind, speak the praises of the Lord, Har Har. Wash the True Guru's feet again and again and worship them: in this way find my Lord God. Lust, anger, greed, attachment, pride and the pleasures of vice: keep (well) away from their company. Joining the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), let us speak of the Lord; (let us) speak with the Saadh (the holy one): the Lord's love is the elixir, the Name of Ram is the elixir; dwell on the Lord, on the Name of Ram, on Ram. The pride and force within, (the conceit that) you know something, something, something: put this away, and take hold of yourself. O Lord, my Master, be merciful to your servant Nanak; O Lord, make (him) dust at the feet of the Sants (saints). ॥2॥
1119.1: Raag Kedara, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mother, (the soul-bride who) has awakened in the company of the Sants beholds the Beloved's wonders, and repeating the Naam she comes to own the treasure (of peace). She thirsts for the sight (of God), and her eyes keep a steady gaze (on him); the thirst for anything else is forgotten. Now (I) have found the Guru, the giver of the peace of Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise); gazing on (him), (my) mind is caught up (in him). Seeing Damodar, joy has welled up in the mind; O Nanak, the Beloved's word is Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life). ॥2॥
Damodar (he whose waist was bound with a cord: the child Krishna) is a name of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; in Gurbani it is a name of the one God.
1119.2: Raag Kedara, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O merciful one, hear the prayer of the meek: the mind is one, a slave to the five (passions), and the three (qualities) are its foes, O Master of the masterless. Save (me from them), O compassionate one. I make many efforts, I go (on pilgrimage), I keep to the way of the six rites (khat karam) and sit fixed in meditation; I have tried every means and am worn out, (yet these) dreadful (foes) do not, do not let up. O Lord of compassion, (I seek your) refuge, (I bow to you) in reverence, O Lord, Har Har Har Hare, who takes away the round of birth and death. You alone, O merciful to the meek, (are my shelter); O God, (your) feet are Nanak's support. (Many) have been carried across the ocean of doubt and attachment, clinging to the feet of the Sants and to the hem (of their robes). ॥2॥
The five: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride. The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas, under which all deeds are done.
The six rites (khat karam): the six duties of a Brahmin: studying and teaching the Vedas, performing and officiating at sacrifice, giving and receiving gifts.
1119.3: Raag Kedara, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Master, treasure (of all), I have come to (your) refuge. Love for the Naam has sprung up within (my) mind; O Lord, (I have come) to beg (it of you) as alms. O giver of peace, perfect Supreme God, in your mercy keep (my) honour. O Master, give (me your) love in the Saadh's company, (that my) tongue may tell the Lord's praises. O Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), merciful Gobind (the Lord of the universe), O Damodar, (grant me) the wisdom of your pure discourse. Dye Nanak in the Lord's love, (and let his) mind be fixed on (your) lotus feet. ॥2॥
1119.4: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In (my) mind is a longing for the sight of the Lord. In your mercy unite (me) with the Sat Sangat, (and) give (me) your Name. O Beloved, may I serve the true ones (the holy); wherever (your praise) is heard, there joy rises in the mind. I am ever a sacrifice to (you), I give myself up, I am devoted; how beyond compare is your dwelling! You cherish all, you take care of all; all are under your shade. O God of Nanak, all-pervading Creator, may I see you alone in every heart. ॥2॥
1120.1: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The love of the Beloved is dear (to me). Absorbed within my mind, I dwell on the hope (of meeting you); my eyes are fixed on you in a steady gaze. What are they like, those days, those watches, those hours and instants? What are they like, those instants, that moment, when the doors are flung open at once, thirst is quenched, and I live on beholding (your) sight? What is that effort, what sort of means, what service shall I think upon (that you may be met)? O Nanak, giving up honour, pride and attachment, (the soul) is saved in the company of the Sants. ॥2॥
1120.2: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sing the praises of the Lord, Har Har Har. Have mercy, O Gopal, O Gobind, and make (me) repeat your Name. O God, you have drawn out of other pleasures (those) whose minds you join to the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy); (for those) to whom you show your sight, doubt, fear and attachment have been cut away by the Guru's word. May my mind become the dust of (the feet of) all; make (me) give up the intellect of ego. Give (me) your devotion, O merciful one; O Nanak, it is by great good fortune that the Lord is found. ॥2॥
1120.3: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without the Lord, life goes to waste. (He who) forsakes Gopal and is absorbed in other pleasures: false is (all he) wears and eats. Wealth, youth, property: (he) enjoys (their) comforts, (but none of them) stands by (him) in the least. The madman, seeing the mirage (the deer's thirst), is caught up in it, dyed in the pleasure of (joys like) the shade of a tree. Bewitched by the great intoxication of pride and attachment, (he lies) in the pit of lust and anger. O revered God, be (his) help, and take your servant Nanak by the hand. ॥2॥
1120.4: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without the Lord, no one will go along (with the soul). (He is) the Lord of the lowly, the Master full of compassion, the Lord of those who have no lord. Sons, wealth and the pleasures of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) that (one) enjoys do not stand by (him) on the road of Jam (the messenger of Death). The Naam is the treasure: sing the praises of Gobind, and rise out of the pit of the (world-)ocean. In the refuge of the all-powerful, indescribable (Lord), beyond the senses, sorrows are lifted as one remembers the Lord. Meek Nanak longs for the dust of the servants' feet; it is found (by one on whose) forehead it is written by the Lord from the start. ॥2॥
1120.5: Raag Kedara, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Lord is not forgotten by (my) mind; now this love has grown mighty, and other pleasures have been burnt away. How could the chatrik forsake the drop? The fish does not live (out of water) for a moment. Utter the praises of Gopal with (your) tongue: (so) this becomes (your) habit. The deer, enticed by the great sound, is pierced by sharp arrows. The lotus feet of God are a store of sweetness; Nanak has tied (his mind to them) in a knot. ॥2॥
The chatrik (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water.
Hunters draw the deer at night with the sound of a bell (ghanda hera); the deer gives up its life to that sound.
1121.1: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Beloved, a hollowness (a flaw) dwells in (my) heart. O Master, remove the wall of doubt, and taking hold of (me) draw (me) to your side. Many are the pits in the world-ocean; in your kindness lift (me) onto the shore. O Lord, in the company of the Sants (your) feet are the ship that takes me up and carries me across. He who sustained (us) in the pit of the womb: in the forest of vice there is no other (to keep us). The Lord is mighty, an all-powerful refuge; Nanak is beholden to no other. ॥2॥
1121.2: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With (your) tongue speak Ram, Ram; utter the praises of Gopal day and night, (and) sins are destroyed. Leaving all wealth behind, (you) must depart; know that death stands over (your) head. Attachment to the false and endless hopes: hold (them) surely to be false. Fix (your) meditation in the heart on the True Being, the Timeless Form. O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure and the profit; this is the merchandise accepted (in the Lord's court). ॥2॥
1121.3: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (He who has) the support of the Lord's Name, no strife or suffering touches (him) at all; (his) dealing is in the company of the Sants. (In him whom God) in his grace has himself protected, no vice springs up. He to whom (this gift) is granted remembers (the Naam); the world (and its fire) does not burn him. Peace, joy and bliss: cherish (in your heart) the Amrit feet of the Lord God, Har Har. Servant Nanak has come to (your) refuge; (he is) dust at your Sants' feet. ॥2॥
1121.4: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without the Lord's Name, cursed are the ears. Those who live forgetting (God), the embodiment of life: what life is theirs? They eat and drink many dishes, (yet are) like donkeys carrying loads. At all hours they endure great toil, like an ox yoked to the oil-press. Those who forsake Gopal and attach themselves to others weep in many ways. With joined palms Nanak begs this gift: that I may keep the Lord strung at my throat. ॥2॥
1121.5: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The soul that) has taken the dust of (the feet of) the Sants and rubbed it on her face, through the virtues of the imperishable, ever-perfect (Lord), the faults of Kalyug (the dark age) do not take hold of (her). Through the Guru's word all (her) tasks are fulfilled; (she) does not waver this way or that. (Seeing) the one God filling the many, everywhere, (she) does not burn in the fire of vice. (God) has taken his servant by the arm (and made him his own); (his) light has merged in the Light. The masterless one has come to the refuge of God's feet; O Nanak, (his soul) walks with the Lord. ॥2॥
1121.6: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (He whose) mind has a relish for the Lord's Name (has) peace a millionfold and perfect bliss; the burning in (his) breast is quenched. Walking on the path of the Sants, mortals, the fallen in great numbers, are saved. When the dust of (the feet of the Lord's) servant touches the forehead, (it brings) the purity of many tiraths (places of pilgrimage). With meditation on (the Lord's) lotus feet within, the Master is seen in every heart. O Nanak, in the refuge of the infinite, radiant Lord, Jam no longer quarrels (with one). ॥2॥
1122.1: Raag Kedara, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Meet (me), O my dear Beloved. He, the Purakh (the all-pervading Being), the Creator, is filling all places, present in all. The Lord (himself) has made the way to God; (it) is known in the company of the Sants. In the company of the Sants the Purakh, the Creator, is known, and is beheld with the eyes in every heart. Whoever comes to (his) refuge finds every comfort; (God) does not let a sesame seed's worth of (his) labour go to waste. (He who) sings (the praises of) the Lord, the treasure of virtues, in the ease of Sahaj, is intoxicated with the supreme delight of love. (O God,) servant Nanak is in your refuge; you are the perfect Purakh, the Creator. The servants pierced through with loving devotion to the Lord: where else could they go? The fish cannot bear separation; without water (fish) die. How can one live without the Lord? Who can bear the pain (of parting)? The chatrik thirsts for the (rain)drop. When will the night pass? The chakvi finds peace (only when) the sun's ray shines forth. Blessed is the day (when) the mind is fixed on the Lord's sight; night and day (his servants) sing the Lord's praises. Servant Nanak offers this prayer: how can the breath of life hold without the Lord? As a body without breath: how can it have any beauty? (so) the holy one, without (the Lord's) sight, cannot rest for an instant. To live without the Lord is to endure hell; (he whose) mind is pierced through by (the Lord's) lotus feet becomes the Lord's lover, a bairagi (one who longs for the Lord), his attention fixed on the Naam, and is nowhere spurned. To go and meet the Lord, to dwell in the Saadh Sangat: that joy is more than the heart can hold. Be merciful, O Master of Nanak, (that he) may merge in the feet of the Lord. Searching and searching, (I) have met God: the Lord has shown compassion. I am without virtue, lowly and masterless, (yet he) did not weigh (my) faults. (He) did not weigh (my) faults, and granted perfect peace; to make (the fallen) pure is told as (his) age-old way. Hearing that (he) loves devotion, (I) have taken hold of the hem of (his robe); (he) is wholly present in every heart. In the ease of Sahaj (I) have found the ocean of peace, and the pains of birth and death are ended. O Nanak, (God) has taken his servants by the hand (and made them his own); the Name of Ram is the necklace on (their) hearts. ॥4॥
The chakvi (ruddy shelduck), parted from her mate at night, waits all night for the sunrise.
1123.1: Raag Kedara, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Praise and slander (of others) are both to be shunned; give up honour and pride. Those who know iron and gold as one and the same are the very image of God (Bhagwan). (O Lord,) rare indeed is the one who is your servant. (He who holds) lust, anger, greed and attachment forbidden: he alone comes to know the state of (union with) the Lord. Rajas, tamas and sattva, as the qualities are called: all this is your Maya. The man who comes to know the fourth state: he alone has attained the supreme state. (Such a one) stays ever free of desire for tiraths, fasts, set rules, ritual purity and restraints; as he dwells on Ram, the Lord within all, craving and the wandering after Maya are ended. In the house where the lamp is lit, there darkness is dispelled; (so, where) the Fearless One fills (the heart), doubt has fled: says Kabir, the slave of (the Lord's) servants. ॥4॥
The fourth state (turiya): the spiritual state beyond Maya's three qualities.
1123.2: One has traded in bronze and copper, another in cloves and betel nuts. O Sants, (I) have traded in the Name of Gobind: such is my cargo. (I am) a dealer in the Lord's Name: into (my) hands has come the priceless diamond, and (my) worldly ways are left behind. When the True One set (them to it), then (they) took to the Truth, dealers in the True One. They set out with loads of the true merchandise, and reached the Keeper of the treasure. (The Lord) himself is the jewel, the gem and the ruby; he himself keeps the shop; he himself sends (the traders) out in the ten directions; the Merchant himself never moves. Making the mind the ox and (my) attention the road, (I) have filled the sack with wisdom and loaded it. Says Kabir: listen, O Sants, my cargo has come safely through. ॥4॥
1123.3: O wine-seller, O rustic, O foolish intellect: I am turning back the restless mind that had turned the wrong way; (my) mind is intoxicated: with a still (set high) as Mount Meru, I draw off the stream of Amrit. O brothers, call out the Name of Ram again and again. Drink (it), O Sants: (it gives) for ever an understanding rarely found, and in Sahaj (it) quenches thirst. Living in (God's) fear, love (is born); through that love some few, (each one who) tastes the Lord's delight, O brother, understand that the Amrit is within every heart, however many; (yet the Lord) gives it to drink to whom he pleases. The one city (of the body) has nine gates: (he who) holds back the mind running (through them) and makes it still, (his) trikuti is undone, the Tenth Gate opens, and then, O brother, the mind is intoxicated. The state free of fear fills (the mind), and there all torments end: so says Kabir, having reflected. Walking the steep, uphill way, this wine has been found, (its) intoxication like that of the wine of grapes. ॥4॥

Kalvari: the woman who distils and sells liquor; Kabir calls his foolish intellect by this name and speaks of the still within. Mer: Sumer (Meru), the golden mountain at the centre of the world in the Puranas.

The nine gates: the nine openings of the body. The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God. Trikuti: the three furrows of a frowning brow, the mind's fretting.
1123.4: In the grip of lust, anger and craving, (people) have not known the state of (union with) the One; their eyes are blinded and (they) see nothing; (they) have drowned and died without water. Why do you walk so crookedly, crookedly, crookedly (in your pride)? (You are) bones and skin stuffed with filth, wrapped in nothing but stench. You do not repeat Ram: what delusion has led you astray? Death is not far from you. With many efforts you keep this body, (but it) is left behind when (its) span is full. Nothing comes of one's own doing: what can any mortal do? When it pleases him, the True Guru is met, (and one) utters the Name of the One alone. You dwell in a little house of sand and swell with pride in the body, O ignorant one. Says Kabir: those who did not keep Ram in mind, however clever, have drowned. ॥4॥
1124.1: (Man) ties his turban askew, walks with a swagger, and takes to chewing betel leaves; (he says:) I have nothing to do with love and devotion; my business is the court. In pride (man) has forgotten Ram. Gazing and gazing on gold and a most beautiful woman, (he) takes them to be lasting. Greed, falsehood, vice and great pride: in these ways (his) life passes. Says Kabir: at the last hour, in the end, death comes and lays hold of (him). ॥2॥
1124.2: For four days (man) beats his own drum (of rule), and then departs. Though (one) earned so much, tied it up in bundles and buried it in the ground, (he) takes nothing with him. The wife sits on the threshold and weeps; the mother goes with (him) as far as the outer gate; all the people and the family go together as far as the cremation ground, (but) the swan (the soul) goes on alone. Those sons, that wealth, those towns and cities: (he) never comes back to see them again. Says Kabir: why do you not remember Ram? (Your) life is going to waste. ॥2॥
Naubat: the great drum beaten at a ruler's gate, a sign of rule.
1124.3: Raag Kedara, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (One who) keeps the six rites and comes of a high family, but has no devotion to the Lord in his heart, (and) does not love to hear of the (Lord's) lotus feet, is the equal of a supach (one held an outcaste), no better. O heedless mind, remember (the Lord), remember (him). Why do you not look at Balmik? Born of what (low) caste, he reached what (high) station! (This is) the excellence of devotion to Ram. (He was) a killer of dogs, of lower birth than all, (yet) he gave his love to Krishna (the Lord). What can the poor world say in (his) praise? (His fame) has spread through the three worlds. Ajamal, Pingula, the hunter and the elephant (all) went to the Lord. If those of such evil mind were carried across, O Ravidas, why would you not cross over? ॥3॥

Supach (one who cooks dogs): a name for the chandal, a caste that those who kept rules of touch counted the lowest. Balmik: in the old tellings a devotee of low caste, raised by devotion to the Lord to the highest honour.

Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called on his son Narayan. Pingula: a courtesan who waited all night for a lover, then turned that love to the Lord and was saved. The hunter: Jara, who shot Krishna in the foot, taking him for a deer. The elephant (Gaj): in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free.

Sing the praises of the Lord, Har Har Har.
Have mercy, O Gopal, O Gobind, and make (me) repeat your Name.
O God, you have drawn out of other pleasures (those) whose minds you join to the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy);
(for those) to whom you show your sight, doubt, fear and attachment have been cut away by the Guru's word.
May my mind become the dust of (the feet of) all; make (me) give up the intellect of ego.
Give (me) your devotion, O merciful one; O Nanak, it is by great good fortune that the Lord is found. ॥2॥
1120.3: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without the Lord, life goes to waste.
(He who) forsakes Gopal and is absorbed in other pleasures: false is (all he) wears and eats.
Wealth, youth, property: (he) enjoys (their) comforts, (but none of them) stands by (him) in the least.
The madman, seeing the mirage (the deer's thirst), is caught up in it, dyed in the pleasure of (joys like) the shade of a tree.
Bewitched by the great intoxication of pride and attachment, (he lies) in the pit of lust and anger.
O revered God, be (his) help, and take your servant Nanak by the hand. ॥2॥
1120.4: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without the Lord, no one will go along (with the soul).
(He is) the Lord of the lowly, the Master full of compassion, the Lord of those who have no lord.
Sons, wealth and the pleasures of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) that (one) enjoys do not stand by (him) on the road of Jam (the messenger of Death).
The Naam is the treasure: sing the praises of Gobind, and rise out of the pit of the (world-)ocean.
In the refuge of the all-powerful, indescribable (Lord), beyond the senses, sorrows are lifted as one remembers the Lord.
Meek Nanak longs for the dust of the servants' feet; it is found (by one on whose) forehead it is written by the Lord from the start. ॥2॥
1120.5: Raag Kedara, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Lord is not forgotten by (my) mind;
now this love has grown mighty, and other pleasures have been burnt away.
How could the chatrik forsake the drop? The fish does not live (out of water) for a moment.
Utter the praises of Gopal with (your) tongue: (so) this becomes (your) habit.
The deer, enticed by the great sound, is pierced by sharp arrows.
The lotus feet of God are a store of sweetness; Nanak has tied (his mind to them) in a knot. ॥2॥
1121.1: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Beloved, a hollowness (a flaw) dwells in (my) heart.
O Master, remove the wall of doubt, and taking hold of (me) draw (me) to your side.
Many are the pits in the world-ocean; in your kindness lift (me) onto the shore.
O Lord, in the company of the Sants (your) feet are the ship that takes me up and carries me across.
He who sustained (us) in the pit of the womb: in the forest of vice there is no other (to keep us).
The Lord is mighty, an all-powerful refuge; Nanak is beholden to no other. ॥2॥
1121.2: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
utter the praises of Gopal day and night, (and) sins are destroyed.
Leaving all wealth behind, (you) must depart; know that death stands over (your) head.
Attachment to the false and endless hopes: hold (them) surely to be false.
Fix (your) meditation in the heart on the True Being, the Timeless Form.
O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure and the profit; this is the merchandise accepted (in the Lord's court). ॥2॥
1121.3: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He who has) the support of the Lord's Name,
no strife or suffering touches (him) at all; (his) dealing is in the company of the Sants.
(In him whom God) in his grace has himself protected, no vice springs up.
He to whom (this gift) is granted remembers (the Naam); the world (and its fire) does not burn him.
Peace, joy and bliss: cherish (in your heart) the Amrit feet of the Lord God, Har Har.
Servant Nanak has come to (your) refuge; (he is) dust at your Sants' feet. ॥2॥
1121.4: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without the Lord's Name, cursed are the ears.
Those who live forgetting (God), the embodiment of life: what life is theirs?
They eat and drink many dishes, (yet are) like donkeys carrying loads.
At all hours they endure great toil, like an ox yoked to the oil-press.
Those who forsake Gopal and attach themselves to others weep in many ways.
With joined palms Nanak begs this gift: that I may keep the Lord strung at my throat. ॥2॥
1121.5: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The soul that) has taken the dust of (the feet of) the Sants and rubbed it on her face,
through the virtues of the imperishable, ever-perfect (Lord), the faults of Kalyug (the dark age) do not take hold of (her).
Through the Guru's word all (her) tasks are fulfilled; (she) does not waver this way or that.
(Seeing) the one God filling the many, everywhere, (she) does not burn in the fire of vice.
(God) has taken his servant by the arm (and made him his own); (his) light has merged in the Light.
The masterless one has come to the refuge of God's feet; O Nanak, (his soul) walks with the Lord. ॥2॥
1121.6: Raag Kedara, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He whose) mind has a relish for the Lord's Name
(has) peace a millionfold and perfect bliss; the burning in (his) breast is quenched.
Walking on the path of the Sants, mortals, the fallen in great numbers, are saved.
When the dust of (the feet of the Lord's) servant touches the forehead, (it brings) the purity of many tiraths (places of pilgrimage).
With meditation on (the Lord's) lotus feet within, the Master is seen in every heart.
O Nanak, in the refuge of the infinite, radiant Lord, Jam no longer quarrels (with one). ॥2॥
1122.1: Raag Kedara, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Meet (me), O my dear Beloved.
He, the Purakh (the all-pervading Being), the Creator, is filling all places, present in all.
The Lord (himself) has made the way to God; (it) is known in the company of the Sants.
In the company of the Sants the Purakh, the Creator, is known, and is beheld with the eyes in every heart.
Whoever comes to (his) refuge finds every comfort; (God) does not let a sesame seed's worth of (his) labour go to waste.
(He who) sings (the praises of) the Lord, the treasure of virtues, in the ease of Sahaj, is intoxicated with the supreme delight of love.
(O God,) servant Nanak is in your refuge; you are the perfect Purakh, the Creator.
The servants pierced through with loving devotion to the Lord: where else could they go?
The fish cannot bear separation; without water (fish) die.
How can one live without the Lord? Who can bear the pain (of parting)? The chatrik thirsts for the (rain)drop.
When will the night pass? The chakvi finds peace (only when) the sun's ray shines forth.
Blessed is the day (when) the mind is fixed on the Lord's sight; night and day (his servants) sing the Lord's praises.
Servant Nanak offers this prayer: how can the breath of life hold without the Lord?
As a body without breath: how can it have any beauty?
(so) the holy one, without (the Lord's) sight, cannot rest for an instant.
To live without the Lord is to endure hell; (he whose) mind is pierced through by (the Lord's) lotus feet
becomes the Lord's lover, a bairagi (one who longs for the Lord), his attention fixed on the Naam, and is nowhere spurned.
To go and meet the Lord, to dwell in the Saadh Sangat: that joy is more than the heart can hold.
Be merciful, O Master of Nanak, (that he) may merge in the feet of the Lord.
Searching and searching, (I) have met God: the Lord has shown compassion.
I am without virtue, lowly and masterless, (yet he) did not weigh (my) faults.
(He) did not weigh (my) faults, and granted perfect peace; to make (the fallen) pure is told as (his) age-old way.
Hearing that (he) loves devotion, (I) have taken hold of the hem of (his robe); (he) is wholly present in every heart.
In the ease of Sahaj (I) have found the ocean of peace, and the pains of birth and death are ended.
O Nanak, (God) has taken his servants by the hand (and made them his own); the Name of Ram is the necklace on (their) hearts. ॥4॥
1123.1: Raag Kedara, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Praise and slander (of others) are both to be shunned; give up honour and pride.
Those who know iron and gold as one and the same are the very image of God (Bhagwan).
(O Lord,) rare indeed is the one who is your servant.
(He who holds) lust, anger, greed and attachment forbidden: he alone comes to know the state of (union with) the Lord.
Rajas, tamas and sattva, as the qualities are called: all this is your Maya.
The man who comes to know the fourth state: he alone has attained the supreme state.
(Such a one) stays ever free of desire for tiraths, fasts, set rules, ritual purity and restraints;
as he dwells on Ram, the Lord within all, craving and the wandering after Maya are ended.
In the house where the lamp is lit, there darkness is dispelled;
(so, where) the Fearless One fills (the heart), doubt has fled: says Kabir, the slave of (the Lord's) servants. ॥4॥
1123.2: One has traded in bronze and copper, another in cloves and betel nuts.
O Sants, (I) have traded in the Name of Gobind: such is my cargo.
(I am) a dealer in the Lord's Name:
into (my) hands has come the priceless diamond, and (my) worldly ways are left behind.
When the True One set (them to it), then (they) took to the Truth, dealers in the True One.
They set out with loads of the true merchandise, and reached the Keeper of the treasure.
(The Lord) himself is the jewel, the gem and the ruby; he himself keeps the shop;
he himself sends (the traders) out in the ten directions; the Merchant himself never moves.
Making the mind the ox and (my) attention the road, (I) have filled the sack with wisdom and loaded it.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants, my cargo has come safely through. ॥4॥
1123.3: O wine-seller, O rustic, O foolish intellect: I am turning back the restless mind that had turned the wrong way;
(my) mind is intoxicated: with a still (set high) as Mount Meru, I draw off the stream of Amrit.
O brothers, call out the Name of Ram again and again.
Drink (it), O Sants: (it gives) for ever an understanding rarely found, and in Sahaj (it) quenches thirst.
Living in (God's) fear, love (is born); through that love some few, (each one who) tastes the Lord's delight, O brother, understand
that the Amrit is within every heart, however many; (yet the Lord) gives it to drink to whom he pleases.
The one city (of the body) has nine gates: (he who) holds back the mind running (through them) and makes it still,
(his) trikuti is undone, the Tenth Gate opens, and then, O brother, the mind is intoxicated.
The state free of fear fills (the mind), and there all torments end: so says Kabir, having reflected.
Walking the steep, uphill way, this wine has been found, (its) intoxication like that of the wine of grapes. ॥4॥
1123.4: In the grip of lust, anger and craving, (people) have not known the state of (union with) the One;
their eyes are blinded and (they) see nothing; (they) have drowned and died without water.
Why do you walk so crookedly, crookedly, crookedly (in your pride)?
(You are) bones and skin stuffed with filth, wrapped in nothing but stench.
You do not repeat Ram: what delusion has led you astray? Death is not far from you.
With many efforts you keep this body, (but it) is left behind when (its) span is full.
Nothing comes of one's own doing: what can any mortal do?
When it pleases him, the True Guru is met, (and one) utters the Name of the One alone.
You dwell in a little house of sand and swell with pride in the body, O ignorant one.
Says Kabir: those who did not keep Ram in mind, however clever, have drowned. ॥4॥
1124.1: (Man) ties his turban askew, walks with a swagger, and takes to chewing betel leaves;
(he says:) I have nothing to do with love and devotion; my business is the court.
Gazing and gazing on gold and a most beautiful woman, (he) takes them to be lasting.
Greed, falsehood, vice and great pride: in these ways (his) life passes.
Says Kabir: at the last hour, in the end, death comes and lays hold of (him). ॥2॥
1124.2: For four days (man) beats his own drum (of rule), and then departs.
Though (one) earned so much, tied it up in bundles and buried it in the ground, (he) takes nothing with him.
The wife sits on the threshold and weeps; the mother goes with (him) as far as the outer gate;
all the people and the family go together as far as the cremation ground, (but) the swan (the soul) goes on alone.
Those sons, that wealth, those towns and cities: (he) never comes back to see them again.
Says Kabir: why do you not remember Ram? (Your) life is going to waste. ॥2॥
1124.3: Raag Kedara, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(One who) keeps the six rites and comes of a high family, but has no devotion to the Lord in his heart,
(and) does not love to hear of the (Lord's) lotus feet, is the equal of a supach (one held an outcaste), no better.
O heedless mind, remember (the Lord), remember (him).
Why do you not look at Balmik?
Born of what (low) caste, he reached what (high) station! (This is) the excellence of devotion to Ram.
(He was) a killer of dogs, of lower birth than all, (yet) he gave his love to Krishna (the Lord).
What can the poor world say in (his) praise? (His fame) has spread through the three worlds.
Ajamal, Pingula, the hunter and the elephant (all) went to the Lord.
If those of such evil mind were carried across, O Ravidas, why would you not cross over? ॥3॥
